evidence: The set-page descriptor is registered by the timer application. Its create callback allocates and stores page state; destroy frees and clears it. The page builder registers callbacks for each picker for filters 9 and 7. The three callbacks only call the corresponding selector when the fetched event code equals 9. The selected helper also updates an optional caption and active picker. The start callback parses all picker strings, checks for a positive duration, and can start a timer.
scope: Only the listed call sites while the page state is nonzero. Selector helpers may also be called by non-LVGL paths; intercepting an event does not prevent all ways to change the selection.
limitations: Picker and timer state may become inconsistent if callbacks are skipped or parameters changed. The caption and page state slots must remain valid; shared entry publication and rollback require system-wide quiescence. Device behavior is unverified.
